about.thesis: I hands-on build the full stack around the model in addition to the SLM and fine-tuning work. The customer interacts with the product, not the model. The product compensates for the model's weaknesses. Building mission-critical applications with AI stack since 2020. Gen AI context management as infrastructure. Evaluation and explainability as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts.
about.arc: I started as an engineer (protocol stacks, Python frameworks, AST-based tooling) and moved into product. I write PRDs. I also read the code behind them. Intrapreneur inside the enterprise: built Fujitsu's first GenAI product from nothing and deployed it across 6 Tier-1 customers globally. Entrepreneur outside: published Smart-Review on the GitHub Marketplace in 2019, ran an Uber fleet management venture in Chennai (2015-2017), built overlay tools for real users with real money on the line. What you see here is what is available in the open. The enterprise work, 6 Tier-1 deployments, EU AI Act compliance, 20% autonomous issue resolution, sits behind NDA.

projects.name: GraspRepo
projects.one_liner: Reverse-engineers how coding agents understand your codebase. Zero AI APIs, pure algorithmic analysis.
projects.problem: Coding agents like Cursor and Copilot analyze codebases using AST parsing and graph algorithms, but that process is invisible. Developers can't see what the agent sees, can't verify its understanding, and can't identify blind spots.
projects.what_it_does: Parses ASTs with Tree-sitter across 20+ languages, builds dependency graphs, runs PageRank to rank file importance, computes code churn via git history, and visualizes everything in a 4-quadrant prioritization matrix. Interactive web dashboard with vis.js graph visualization.
projects.why_it_matters: Makes the invisible visible. The same interpretability problem that exists in LLMs exists in coding agents. If you can't see what it sees, you can't trust it. This tool solves that.
projects.what_i_learned: Interpretability is a product requirement, not a research luxury. Built the scoring from scratch: PageRank for structural importance, churn for change frequency, hotspot detection where the two intersect.
projects.architecture_notes: 5 analysis stages: AST parsing, dependency graph, PageRank ranking, code churn (6-month lookback), prioritization matrix. Hotspot score = normalized PageRank * normalized commits.
projects.results: 5 analysis stages. 20+ languages supported. Pre-cached example repos. GitHub OAuth for custom repos. Deployed on Render.

projects.name: Visual Learning: Context Management in AI Apps
projects.one_liner: Interactive visual explainer for how AI apps manage context around stateless LLMs.
projects.problem: LLMs are stateless. They remember nothing between API calls. The application layer (not the model) maintains conversation history, manages context windows, and creates the illusion of memory. Most developers don't understand this.
projects.what_it_does: 5-tab interactive SPA: The Problem (context rot, Lost in the Middle), Context Window Visualizer (toggle between ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Cursor, Aider allocations), 5 Strategies (full replay, sliding window, summarization, RAG, hybrid), Aider Deep Dive (Tree-sitter + PageRank verified architecture), and an Interactive Chat Simulator with scripted conversation showing live token allocation.
projects.why_it_matters: Building with LLMs is 95% traditional software engineering and 5% AI-specific. Context management IS the product differentiation. This tool makes that visible and teachable.
projects.what_i_learned: The 'Alice layer', the application around the model, is where all the product decisions live. Teaching this required building it interactively, not writing about it.
projects.architecture_notes: Single-page app, no frameworks. Token estimation: max(50, round(text.length / 3.5)). Simulator tracks system tokens, history, RAG, and current turn in real-time. 7-step scripted conversation with 3 options per turn.
projects.results: Covers 5 major AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Cursor, Aider) with real architectural details. Interactive simulator with live context window visualization.
projects.related_writing: Based on concepts from Thinking in Analogies: A Generative AI Playbook for Tech Professionals

projects.name: Smart-Review
projects.one_liner: Intelligently add code reviewer. GitHub Marketplace launch (2019-2020). Opensourced the entire stack.
projects.problem: Code review relies on static hierarchies or CODEOWNERS files, missing engineers with actual hands-on experience of the code being modified. 4 out of 5 real PRs analyzed showed expertise gaps, with regressions within 12-25 days proving the point.
projects.what_it_does: Analyzes git history for affected files to compute expertise and seniority scores. Expertise: ownership 40%, commits 25%, lines 15%, recency 20%. Seniority: tenure 45%, commits 30%, consistency 25%. 5 real PRs analyzed from rails, react, huggingface/transformers, prometheus. Original 2019 version was a Probot app published in GitHub Marketplace with PyDriller-based reviewer.py engine.
projects.why_it_matters: A 7-year arc on the same problem. Built pre-LLM in 2019 with pattern matching and heuristics, rebuilt in 2026 as full-stack with real data proving the thesis. 4 out of 5 PRs show the assigned reviewer wasn't the best choice.
projects.what_i_learned: The constraints of pre-LLM automation made the value of LLMs concrete later. But this problem doesn't even need an LLM. Just smart use of git history data already in the repo.
projects.architecture_notes: Monorepo: apps/web (React frontend), apps/api (FastAPI backend), packages/analysis (reusable scoring + mining). PyDriller walks git history of affected files, extracts per-author metrics, computes weighted scores. GitHub handle resolution via commit search API.
projects.results: DevTool Entrepreneurship. 4 show expertise gaps (regressions within 12-25 days). ~30-100 contributors scored per PR. Phase 2 backend ready: OAuth, live PR analysis, rate limiting, caching.

projects.name: CricketMind
projects.one_liner: Fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron-Mini-4B for cricket domain expertise. Improved model performance on a subset of cricket knowledge from 30.2% to 67.5%.
projects.problem: No existing LLM understood cricket deeply enough, the Laws, the strategy, the edge cases. Domain adaptation shouldn't need massive budgets.
projects.what_it_does: LoRA fine-tuning (rank 16, alpha 32) with response distillation using Claude as teacher model. 170 training examples (laws QA + match situation analysis). Custom CricketBench evaluation suite: 20 questions across 4 weighted categories (Laws Recall 30%, Conditional Reasoning 35%, Match Situation 25%, Edge Case 10%), scored by Claude Sonnet as LLM-as-judge.
projects.why_it_matters: Proves that domain-adapted LLMs don't need massive budgets. Evaluation-driven training: built CricketBench first, then trained to beat it. The benchmark defined the goal, not the other way around.
projects.what_i_learned: Largest gains in conditional reasoning (+45pp) and match situation analysis (+50pp). Distillation teaches decomposition skills, not just memorization. Data quality gates (~10% rejection rate) matter more than data quantity. Published a 6-part Substack series documenting the entire journey.
projects.architecture_notes: Pipeline: MCC Laws text, Claude distillation, quality gates, LoRA fine-tuning (3 epochs, 35 min on A100), merge adapters, GGUF export, CricketBench evaluation. Runs locally via Ollama.
projects.results: 67.5% weighted accuracy vs 30.2% baseline (+37.3pp). Conditional reasoning: +45pp. Match situation: +50pp. 170 training examples. 35 minutes training time.
projects.related_writing: Building CricketMind: An AI Product Manager's Journey Through the Model Layer (6-part Substack series)

projects.name: CIAL: Crypto Intelligence Abstraction Layer
projects.one_liner: Enterprise-grade crypto intelligence platform. Real-time streaming, multi-tier caching, full observability.
projects.problem: Crypto intelligence requires real-time data aggregation from multiple sources, low-latency delivery to thousands of concurrent clients, and enterprise-grade reliability. Most crypto tools are either toy demos or closed-source platforms.
projects.what_it_does: Intelligence Broker pattern for routing data to AI agents. Agent Registry for coordination. Dual Memory System: Redis (short-term) + PostgreSQL (long-term). Multi-tier caching (L1 Memory + L2 Redis = 96% faster). WebSocket streaming to 10K+ concurrent clients. JWT auth + API keys + per-endpoint rate limiting. Full observability: Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, Sentry errors, structured logging.
projects.why_it_matters: Enterprise AI infrastructure built from scratch, not a wrapper around an API. Shows the full stack: data ingestion, caching, streaming, security, observability. One-click deploy to Render.
projects.what_i_learned: The infrastructure around AI agents, memory, routing, caching, observability, is where most teams fail. The agent itself is the easy part. Building the reliable delivery layer is the real engineering.
projects.architecture_notes: 3-tier: Application (FastAPI + WebSocket + Security), Infrastructure (PostgreSQL + pgvector + Redis + Kafka + TimescaleDB), Observability (Prometheus + Grafana + Sentry + Structlog). Phase 1: Foundation. Phase 2: Scale. Phase 3 planned: ML anomaly detection, LSTM prediction, sentiment analysis.
projects.results: 10K+ concurrent WebSocket connections. 96% cache hit improvement with multi-tier caching. 100x faster time-series queries with TimescaleDB. One-click Render deploy.

projects.name: Metabolistic Storyteller
projects.one_liner: Full-stack metabolic analytics platform with glucose-migraine causal chain visualization backed by 6 peer-reviewed citations.
projects.problem: Most health analytics show correlations and call them insights. The glucose-migraine connection, nocturnal hypoglycemia triggering hormonal cascade leading to morning migraine, is a documented causal chain that no consumer tool visualizes.
projects.what_it_does: React + FastAPI + TimescaleDB platform. 3 demo profiles with 90 days of pre-computed insights each. Multi-layer metabolic overlay (CGM + sleep + exercise + nutrition on one chart with auto-detected pattern callouts). Migraine timeline with hourly glucose curves, event strips, and per-day narratives. 15-day time-series views. ML pipeline: PCMCI causal discovery, STUMPY pattern detection, association rules. JWT auth, CSV/Excel upload wizard, background Celery tasks.
projects.why_it_matters: The first consumer tool showing the nocturnal hypo to hormonal cascade to morning migraine causal chain, backed by 6 peer-reviewed citations. Moves beyond correlation dashboards to actual causal explanation.
projects.what_i_learned: Health data requires causal reasoning, not just pattern matching. PCMCI for causal discovery and STUMPY for time-series pattern detection are underused in consumer health tools. The narrative layer, turning statistics into a personal story, is what makes data actionable.
projects.architecture_notes: React frontend, FastAPI backend, TimescaleDB (time-series), Celery + Redis (background jobs), ML pipeline (PCMCI causal discovery + STUMPY pattern detection + association rules). 19 end-to-end tests.
projects.results: 3 demo profiles with 90 days of insights. Glucose-migraine causal chain backed by 6 citations. 19 end-to-end tests. Deployed on Render.

projects.name: IntelliYANG
projects.one_liner: AI-powered chatbot for querying OpenROADM YANG network models. Hybrid RAG with multi-stage validation.
projects.problem: OpenROADM YANG models are complex, deeply nested, and hard to navigate. Network engineers need fast answers about model structure, constraints, and relationships without reading thousands of lines of YANG.
projects.what_it_does: Parses .yang files and extracts semantic chunks (containers, groupings, identities). Hybrid retrieval: vector search + BM25 keyword search. Multi-stage validation pipeline (syntax, semantics, optical constraints, confidence threshold at 0.90). Rich CLI interface with session management.
projects.why_it_matters: Bridges the gap between AI capabilities and domain-specific network modeling. RAG applied to a structured, hierarchical data format, not just flat text. Validation pipeline ensures answers are grounded in actual YANG model definitions.
projects.what_i_learned: RAG on structured data (YANG models) requires semantic chunking, not naive text splitting. The validation pipeline is the product. Without it, the chatbot hallucinates plausible-sounding but incorrect network configurations.
projects.architecture_notes: YANG processor (semantic chunking), dual retrieval (vector + BM25), LLM generation, multi-stage validation (syntax, semantics, optical constraints, confidence gate at 0.90), Rich CLI output.
projects.results: Processes full OpenROADM YANG model suite. 0.90 confidence threshold for answer escalation.

projects.name: MCP Learning Resources
projects.one_liner: Interactive visualizations for understanding Model Context Protocol. JSON-RPC message flows and architecture state machines.
projects.problem: MCP is a new protocol and most developers learn it by reading specs. Interactive visualization makes the protocol's message exchanges and lifecycle tangible.
projects.what_it_does: Two interactive HTML tools: (1) JSON-RPC Message Visualization with 5 complete scenarios (initialization, tools, execution, resources, prompts), live message flow animation, color-coded request/response. (2) MCP Architecture State Machine with client-server diagrams, connection lifecycle, capability negotiation, protocol versioning.
projects.why_it_matters: Connects 18 years of MxN integration experience to the MCP philosophy. Built to support the From MxN to MCP article series.
projects.what_i_learned: The MxN integration problem I fought in platform engineering is exactly what MCP solves for AI. The protocol patterns are familiar. The context is new.
projects.architecture_notes: Static HTML files, no server required. Open in any browser.
projects.results: 5 complete protocol scenarios. Interactive state machine visualization.
